sections.label: Pallavi
sections.ta:
தெருவிலே திரிவதில் காண்பார் சிறுமை
கருவிலே குறைபாடோ அறியாரவர் அருமை
sections.translit:
theruvilE thirivadhil kANbAr siRumai
karuvilE kuRaipAdO aRiyAravar arumai
sections.en: Some people find it demeaning that Siva wanders the streets, begging for alms. I wonder if it is a kind of blindness that prevents them from recognizing His greatness.

sections.label: Anupallavi
sections.ta:
உருவிலே பெண் தாங்கும் ஐயன் பெருமை
இருளிலே அறியாது புலம்புவதே வெறுமை
sections.translit:
uruvilE peN thAngum aiyan perumai
iruLilE aRiyAdhu pulambuvadhE veRumai
sections.en: The Lord is eminent—He who bears His consort as part of His own being. Complaints about Him perhaps arise from darkness in the mind and emptiness in one’s thought process.

sections.label: Charanam
sections.ta:
செருவிலே திரிபுரமெரித்த தீரன் அவன்
பருவத்தே உயிர் தந்து காத்திடும் சிவன்
குருவிலே உயர்ந்த சாமகான நாதன்
திருவிலே நீறணிந்து ஆலமர்ந்த போதன்
sections.translit:
seruvilE thiripuramerittha thIran avan
paruvatthE uyir thandhu kAtthidum sivan
guruvilE uyarndha sAmagAna nAdhan
thiruvilE nIRaNindhu Alamarndha bOdhan
sections.en: He is a brave warrior who destroyed the three cities and the demons. He is the Supreme Being who grants life at the opportune moment, like when He kicked Yama and saved the young Markandeya. He is the greatest teacher and a master of Sama Veda music. He smears sacred white ash all over His body and is seated beneath a banyan tree, imparting wisdom even to saints and rishis.

notes: This song contains references to four mythological stories. The first line of the Pallavi refers to the story of Shiva cutting off the fifth head of Brahma to remove his ego. Brahma’s skull then became stuck to Shiva’s hand, and Shiva, overwhelmed by insatiable hunger, wandered about begging for alms. Although some may laugh at Shiva’s plight, his intention (to break Brahma’s pride) is a noble one. For details, see: Uthamar Temple Sthalapuranam Harasaba Vimochana Perumal Temple Sthalapuranam The Anupallavi refers to Shiva offering part of his body to Parvati. This is believed to have occurred at Tiruvannamalai Temple. It is also associated with the time Lord Shiva took the form of a column of fire to establish his supremacy among the Trinity. By adorning his consort as part of himself, Shiva became Ardhanarishvara on the day of Karthigai Deepam. For more details, see: Shiva offered half his body to Parvati. There are other mythological traditions associated with this shrine. When Shiva appeared as a column of fire, no one, including the celestials, could withstand the intense heat. Out of compassion, the Lord transformed himself into a mountain, now known as the Arunachala Hill. The day Shiva offered half of his body to Goddess Parvati is now celebrated as the festival of Karthigai. For less known facts on Tiruvannamalai temple, see: அறிந்த ஆலயங்கள் அபூர்வ தகவல்கள், விகடன் பிரசுரம், 757 அண்ணா சாலை, சென்னை 600002, விற்பனை பிரிவு போன்: 091-44-42634283/ 84, முதற் பதிப்பு: பிப்ரவரி 2008, பக்கம் 38 – 49. Line 1 of the charanam describes Siva destroying the three cities occupied by the three demon brothers. Arunagirinathar, in the Thiruppugazh stanza beginning with “பரதத்தை அடக்கி நடிப்பவர் திரிபுரத்தை எரிக்க நகைப்பவர்பாவைக்குள் விடத்தை மிடற்று இடுபவர் தேர் கப்பரை உற்ற கரத்தர்...”, had established the prowess of Siva in warfare. Siva burnt the city of Thripuram to ashes by simply laughing. For details, including the Tamil and English translations of Thiruppugazh lines, see: Siva burnt the Tricity with a laugh The Thiruppugazh verses beginning with “கரியிணை கோடென...” also allude to Siva burning Thiripuram. Line 2 of the Charanam refers to Shiva saving the life of the young Markandeya when his time had come and the God of Death had arrived to take him. This episode highlights Shiva’s compassion in protecting Markandeya. This incident, in which Shiva conquered Yama to save Markandeya, is believed to have occurred at Triprangode Temple, Mallapuram District, Kerala where Shiva is worshipped as Kalasamhara Murthy. Siva kicks Yama It is also said to have taken place at Thirukkadaiyur Temple in Tamilnadu near Karaikal where Shiva is worshipped as Amritaghateswarar and his consort as Abhirami.
